classification.difficultyReason: Find a partition satisfying simultaneous constraints on the number of squares, the sum of side lengths and the sum of squared side lengths.

inlines.text: You have eight squares with side lengths from 1 to 8. Split them into two groups such that:
each group has the same number of squares,
each group has the same total perimeter,
each group has the same total area.

spec.sourceRegion: Right column, illustration beneath question 14 conditions.
spec.description: Eight unlabelled squares in increasing order, sharing a bottom baseline and separated by gaps. Source cyan fills are omitted under the house unshaded-diagram convention.
spec.mathematics: Square side lengths are proportional to 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8.
spec.answerVisibility: All eight squares are permanent givens; no partition is shown.

answer.short:
Side lengths $\{2,3,5,8\}$ and $\{1,4,6,7\}$.

Each group contains four squares, has total perimeter $72$ and total area $102$.
answer.worked:
Each group needs four squares. Equal total perimeters require equal sums of side lengths; equal total areas require equal sums of their squares.

Choose side lengths $\{2,3,5,8\}$ and $\{1,4,6,7\}$.

The total perimeters are
$$\begin{align*}
P_1&=4(2+3+5+8)\\
P_1&=72\\
P_2&=4(1+4+6+7)\\
P_2&=72.
\end{align*}$$
The total areas are
$$\begin{align*}
A_1&=2^2+3^2+5^2+8^2\\
A_1&=4+9+25+64\\
A_1&=102\\
A_2&=1^2+4^2+6^2+7^2\\
A_2&=1+16+36+49\\
A_2&=102.
\end{align*}$$
Both groups contain four squares, so all three conditions hold.
